reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: All 3 gates passed. The SECURITY DEFINER function `attendance.record_attendance_by_card` is callable by `authenticated` users because `0001_create_attendance_schema.sql:10` sets `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES … GRANT ALL ON FUNCTIONS TO … authenticated`, and the fix migration (`20260317000001`) only explicitly grants EXECUTE to `anon` while never revoking it from `authenticated` — leaving authenticated with inherited EXECUTE. The function runs as postgres (bypasses RLS entirely) with no `current_role()` guard, so any logged-in user can insert forged attendance rows for any card ID they supply. An attacker can trigger this via the Supabase REST API by calling `supabase.rpc('record_attendance_by_card', { p_card_id: '<target_card_id>' })` as any authenticated session, causing the SECURITY DEFINER function to insert an arbitrary attendance record into `attendance.attendances` on behalf of any registered cardholder — compromising the integrity of all attendance data.
